standard_prerequisites.name: Formal glueing of modules and algebras over a finite product of localizations
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, Lemma more-algebra-lemma-application-formal-glueing (canonical Stacks tag 0ALK) and More on Algebra, Remark more-algebra-remark-formal-glueing-algebras (canonical Stacks tag 05EU); invoked at proof lines 548-555
standard_prerequisites.use: Supply the existence of the A-module map and the algebra structure on the glued module; the reduction of the hypothesis to their input, i.e. the flatness of A -> A' with A/I = A'/IA', is inside the counted span.

core_obligations: Reduce to the input of formal glueing: with I = m_1 cap ... cap m_r, A_i = A_{m_i} and A' = prod A_i, verify that IA' = prod m_i A_i and that A -> A' is a flat ring map with A/I isomorphic to A'/IA', which turns the family of local ring maps phi_i into a glueing problem (proof lines 544-548).
Glue the underlying map: apply the formal glueing lemma to obtain an A-module map phi : A -> B whose localization at m_i is isomorphic to phi_i (proof lines 548-551).

Upgrade to a ring map and read off the properties: use the discussion of the glueing remark to endow B with an A-algebra structure matching the given A-algebra structures on the B_i, and then deduce the final assertion from Ker(phi)_{m_i} = Ker(phi_i) and Coker(phi)_{m_i} = Coker(phi_i), so that a power of each m_i annihilates the local pieces and hence a power of I annihilates Ker(phi) and Coker(phi) (proof lines 552-558).
proof_roadmap: Set I, A_i and A' = prod A_i and check the two hypotheses of formal glueing: IA' = prod m_i A_i and A -> A' flat with A/I = A'/IA' (proof lines 544-548).
Glue the modules along the formal glueing lemma to get phi : A -> B localizing to the given phi_i (proof lines 548-551).
Use the glueing remark to make B an A-algebra, and conclude the finite/injective/surjective alternatives from the isomorphisms of the localizations of kernel and cokernel (proof lines 552-558).
difficulty_reason: The lemma reconstructs a single ring map phi : A -> B from finitely many local ring maps phi_i : A_{m_i} -> B_i at pairwise distinct maximal ideals, with the requirement that the kernel and cokernel of phi are killed by a power of the intersection m_1 cap ... cap m_r, and it asks that finiteness, injectivity or surjectivity of all phi_i pass to phi (statement lines 527-540). The non-formal step is the reduction: the product A' = prod A_i satisfies IA' = prod m_i A_i and A -> A' is flat with A/I isomorphic to A'/IA', which is exactly what allows more-algebra-lemma-application-formal-glueing to be invoked and then more-algebra-remark-formal-glueing-algebras to put an A-algebra structure on the glued module (proof lines 546-555). The last observation, that Ker(phi)_{m_i} and Coker(phi)_{m_i} compute the local kernels and cokernels, is what converts the local hypotheses into the global statement. The claim is H2: short and citation-driven, but with one genuine reduction specific to the finitely many maximal ideals.
